newsitem.title: EGYPT: Kuwaiti tried to blame son's death on Iraqis.
newsitem.headline: Kuwaiti tried to blame son's death on Iraqis.

text.p: A Kuwaiti woman was so afraid of her husband's wrath that she tried to blame her son's accidental drowning on the Iraqis, police said on Wednesday.
Egyptian police were called to the Cairo hotel room by the woman, Nemat Abdullah Saoud al-Mukhaizem, early on Tuesday and found the dead body of four-year-old Bassam Badr el-Zawawi.
Notes on the wall and furniture said: "This is an Iraqi message to Kuwait's (Emir Sheikh) Jaber" al-Ahmad al-Sabah.
Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990, but was ejected in the 1991 Gulf War by an international coalition. United Nations sanctions on Baghdad have been in force since August, 1990.

"Questioning of the mother...showed that she found the body of her son drowned in the bath tub," Major General Ahmed Hammam Attiya told reporters. "She dragged him out, put him on the bed, ...and wrote the two sentences in fear of being charged with negligence and of her husband."
The coroner said the boy died of asphyxiation from drowning.
The prosecutor's office will question Mukhaizem but security sources said she was not expected to be charged. "She is going to leave the country tomorrow," one source said.
The family was on holiday in Egypt.
